The port is complete and green: **773/773 tests passing** across all 6 test files.

## What was built

`ported_implementation/src/` mirrors the Python package module-for-module (kebab-case filenames, camelCase identifiers):

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| Entry | `index.ts`, `gbnf.ts` |
| `grammar-graph/` | `graph.ts`, `graph-node.ts`, `graph-pointer.ts`, `parse-state.ts`, `generic-set.ts`, `rule-ref.ts`, `types.ts`, `type-guards.ts`, `get-serialized-rule-key.ts`, `get-input-as-code-points.ts`, `get-parent-stack-id.ts`, `print.ts`, `colorize.ts` |
| `grammar-parser/` | `build-rule-stack.ts` |
| `rules-builder/` | `rules-builder.ts`, `symbol-ids.ts`, `parse-char.ts`, `parse-name.ts`, `parse-space.ts`, `is-word-char.ts`, `types.ts`, `type-guards.ts` |
| `utils/` | `is-point-in-range.ts`, `errors/{build-error-position,get-input-as-string,grammar-parse-error,input-parse-error}.ts` |

Plus `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.unit.ts`, and the suite copied to `tests/` per the suite README.

## Porting notes

- The reference has several comments flagging places where the Python was itself emulating JS semantics — those became natural again: `parseInt(x, 16)` → `NaN`, `is_word_char(None)` testing the literal string `"undefined"`, falsy-string loop guards in `buildErrorPosition`, and `undefined` rendering as `"undefined"` in error lines.
- `GenericSet` and `NodeSet` are identity-based in Python (keyed on `id()`); in TS those are plain `Set`/`Map` on object identity, so `_iterate_over_pointers`' `Dict[int, ...]` keyed by `id(rule)` became a `Map<UnresolvedRule, ...>`.
- Rule classes keep exactly the own properties `type`/`value` so vitest's `toEqual` matches the plain object literals in the tests, and `JSON.stringify(rule)` reproduces the `json.dumps(rule.__dict__)` dedup key in `ParseState.rules()`.
- Empty-`dict` falsiness in `Graph`'s root lookups became explicit `size === 0` checks (an empty `Map` is truthy in JS).

## Verification beyond the suite

I diffed the TS output against the Python reference on surfaces the tests don't touch — `Graph.print()` node layout, `ParseState.size`/`grammar`, code-point-array input, `InputParseError.src`/`errorForMostRecentInput`, and multi-line `GrammarParseError` carets. Output was byte-identical.

One gap to flag: `tsc` isn't installed and the npm registry is blocked in this environment, so nothing type-checked the sources — vitest's esbuild transform strips types without verifying them. I reviewed the annotations by hand and fixed two spots that would have failed `strict` (a divergent `valid` getter/setter pair, and a `Range` tuple inferred as `number[]` in `build-rule-stack.ts`), but a `tsc --noEmit` run is still worth doing once dependencies are installable.
